comments.text:
Call with Dustin
Reviewed the new pricing structure and Reserve pricing calculator. Shared the Spotted Duck wine list and latest web app version. Discussed the Somm program and SommCon.

Discussed Ron’s market values. We increased the market value coverage from 70% to 80% and are testing ways to fill the remaining gaps. Dustin trusts Wine-Searcher the most, particularly when filtering for currently available California market values rather than using preset values. Ron’s cellar is currently showing around $450K in market value with approximately 20% of values still missing. Dustin believes the true value is closer to $750K.

Dustin will share our newsletter with his subscribers, and we will feature him in ours as well.

Dustin shared that Marc Barmazel will be installing a new 10K-capacity cellar and would like to use CellarEye instead of CellarTracker. We also briefly discussed Addison.

Next Steps / Afterthoughts
    Coordinate newsletters and cross-promotions.
    Set Dustin up with a Somm Manager account.
    Present how we’d like to feature Dustin’s profile as part of our Somm program. Explore how we can also support his new restaurant channel. He is a strong example of a retailer, private collector cellar consultant, and hospitality wine consultant.
    Dustin is planning to attend SommCon with us. Revisit and coordinate once we have a clearer plan.
    Discuss whether we can convert more of his current cellars from CellarTracker to CellarEye, or if it makes sense to leave them as is.

Had call today.....

Cellar Conversion Strategy & Customer Outreach — Dustin (Meritage)
Aug 18, 2026 | Attendees: Dustin, Mark, Danielle

Summary:
Discussed the Mark Barmazel investor cellar opportunity, the economics of converting Dustin's existing 10 clients, and a plan for new client acquisition via enewsletter and retail display. Also, discussed potential event at shop around SommCon.

- Mark Barmazel: offer to come from Mostafa/CellarEye (not Dustin) once he signs with a cellar construction company; still a ways out, two companies bidding. His ~7 homes are already on CellarTracker. Pivoting from camera install (only 60-70% coverage) to 3D mapping.
- Existing 10 clients: labor cost, not software resistance, is the real barrier. A 4,000-bottle cellar runs roughly 3 days x 2 people x $75/hr, about $3,600. Scaled across the top 10 clients, that's an estimated 10-15 days of labor, or $20-30K total to convert. A reimbursement model was floated but wasn't enough to offset lost wine-sales time. Decision: don't push mass conversion right now, focus on new client acquisition instead.
- Campaign plan: email blast to the Santa Barbara + San Diego list (Friday/Saturday send), audience includes both consumers, somms and restaurants, promo offer TBD (leaning 6 months free for CellarTracker converts, 3 months for new users, through year end), need a retail display kit for Dustin's shop, priority personal outreach to investors (Jay Flatley, Omid?, Mark Barmazel), and a possible SommCon demo event at Dustin's shop.

Next steps:
1. Create an email introducing CellarEye (Fri/Sat send, video or updated website link); leads route through Dustin first, then to Danielle
2. Finalize promo offer terms (6 months/3 months, through EOY)
3. Create a retail display kit for Dustin's shop
4. Plan SommCon demo event at Dustin's location, Mark has bagel friend who may cater, possibly do an event with Addison
5. Figure out subscription for Marc B., per Anthony was supposed to be included as part of his investment
